definition: Estimating the 3D or 2D joint positions of a hand from images, enabling gesture interfaces, AR manipulation, and sign-language analysis.
details: Estimating the 3D or 2D joint positions of a hand from images, enabling gesture interfaces, AR manipulation, and sign-language analysis.

explainer.lead: Hand pose estimation turns an image of a hand into the 2D or 3D positions of its joints. This gives software a usable description of the hand's shape and position, supporting gesture controls, AR manipulation, and sign-language analysis.

tiers.eli5: Imagine putting small stickers on the joints of a hand and asking a computer where each sticker is in a photo. Hand pose estimation does something similar without the stickers, producing a map of the hand that a computer can use to understand gestures or control virtual objects.
tiers.practitioner: A system takes an image as input and predicts hand-joint coordinates in image space or 3D space. Those coordinates can feed gesture-recognition logic, AR object manipulation, or sign-language analysis; the output representation must match the application's need for 2D or 3D positions.
tiers.paperLevel: Given an image I, hand pose estimation learns or applies a function f such that P = f(I), where P contains the estimated positions of the hand joints. Each position is represented either as a 2D image coordinate, p_j = (u_j, v_j), or as a 3D coordinate, p_j = (x_j, y_j, z_j).

explainer.example: An AR application receives an image of a user's hand, estimates its joint positions in 3D, and uses that hand configuration to support manipulation of a virtual object.

usedIn.name: Gesture interfaces
usedIn.detail: Joint positions provide a description of the hand that can be used to interpret gestures.

usedIn.name: Augmented-reality manipulation
usedIn.detail: Estimated hand poses can support interaction with virtual objects.

usedIn.name: Sign-language analysis
usedIn.detail: Hand-joint positions supply a structured representation of hand configuration for analysis.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating a hand image as a collection of pixels, the system summarizes it as a set of connected joint locations. That compact representation describes the hand's configuration in a form software can act on.
howItWorks: Provide an image containing a hand.
Estimate the position of each hand joint.
Express the positions as 2D image coordinates or 3D coordinates.
Pass the resulting hand pose to a gesture, AR, or sign-language application.
explainer.whyItMatters: It lets applications work with a structured description of a hand rather than raw pixels alone. That makes hand movements useful as input for interaction and analysis.
misconceptions: It estimates joint positions; it does not by itself assign a meaning or label to a gesture.
A 2D pose gives positions in the image, while a 3D pose also represents spatial depth.

diagram.caption: A hand image is converted into joint coordinates, which downstream applications can use.
